block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: Total cost is broader than the advertised property price. For ready-property buyers, compare registration, agency, financing, developer, service, furnishing or fit-out and other applicable costs on the same basis. Use current transaction-specific figures so a cheaper headline price does not hide a more expensive overall purchase.

items.question: How do I compare total cost?

items.answer: The final purchase price can differ materially from the advertised property price. Include registration, agency, trustee, developer, valuation and other applicable transaction expenses rather than using one fee as the total.
items.question: What can affect the final purchase price?

items.answer: Avoiding overpayment starts with comparing the property against credible alternatives. Check how much liquidity remains after the transaction so the purchase does not consume cash needed for fees, delays or unexpected costs.
items.question: How do I avoid overpaying?

items.answer: A limited budget works best when the trade-offs are chosen deliberately. Identify whether a cheaper option gives up location quality, layout, delivery certainty, demand or another feature that matters to the buyer.
items.question: How do I buy with a limited budget?

items.answer: A low entry price is useful only when the reason for the discount is understood. A lower price is offset by weaker location, layout, quality, service costs or resale depth. Protect the overall buying case rather than stretching to a headline price, discount or low initial payment.
